To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interference effects between the allowed and the forbidden components in LO-phonon scattering can be observed in zincblende semiconductors and that they can be used as a sensitive tool for the study of scattering mechanisms in these materials.

(a) the scattering amplitude of a phonon in zincblende crystals depends on the direction of propagation, (b) this scattering amplitude changes sign in going between two directions, and (c) the change is due to an allowed-forbidden interference.

(i) the allowed component of the scattering by LO phonon is not diagonal in the (001) surface, but it is diagonal in the (111) surface; (ii) the forbidden component is always diagonal in both surfaces; (iii) the interference between the allowed and forbidden components takes place only in the (001); and (iv) the interference effects decrease for impure crystals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of phonons and their interactions in semiconductors by means of Raman scattering techniques.
the study of the scattering of electrons by LO phonons.
the study of the electronic structure and of the transport properties of semiconductor nanostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interference effects in the resonant scattering of LO phonons in semiconductors are not only interesting from a theoretical point of view but also have a practical relevance.

, for zincblende-type crystals, there are two different mechanisms for the scattering of an electron by a LO phonon: one, the allowed one, due to the deformation potential; the other, the forbidden one, due to Fröhlich interaction.
, for a (001) zincblende-type crystal, the scattering amplitudes for the [0111 and [0111 polarizations are the same.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the forbidden scattering is the dominant one in GaAs and that in InSb the allowed scattering is the dominant component.
the forbidden scattering is always diagonal and that the allowed component can be diagonal or non-diagonal, the latter being the case for the (001) surface.
the scattering amplitude for LO phonons is not a simple scalar but a 3 x 3 matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
interference effects between allowed and forbidden scattering can be used to identify forbidden scattering.
the forbidden component, which is usually neglected, can play an important role, and that it is necessary to take it into account to interpret the experimental data.
the forbidden component, which is always diagonal, is not negligible in zincblende semiconductors, even for low impurity concentrations.
